notes:
**Five new things you can just say.** Price levels ("buy when nifty crosses 24500"), sides of a moving average ("price above ema 20"), N-bar breaks ("20 bar high break"), gaps ("gap up 1%") and days of the week ("only on monday and friday").

None of these are new capability. The engine could already evaluate all five, correctly, with tests - and nothing in the app could produce one, because the only thing that builds a rule is the sentence parser and the parser knew six conditions out of fifteen. They were built and wired to nothing.

**A side of a moving average is kept apart from a cross.** Being above an EMA is true all the way up a run; crossing it is true on exactly one bar. That is the difference between one trade and forty.

**Two rule engines became one.** There were two implementations of every condition. They agreed - which is exactly why nobody noticed when one of them drifted, twice this week. Now there is one place a condition can be wrong.

**Every template is tested to actually fire**, at all five candle sizes. That is the check the Opening Range Breakout template needed and never had.
